```markdown
# Batch Tracking: Mash Day to Bottle

## Intent
Any bottle in a customer's hand can be traced back to its batch, and that
batch to the supplier lot number of every malt and hop sack that went into
it. The owner has run the brewery for twelve years and settled what they
want in the design conversation. This document records it.

## Goals
- Record each batch from mash day through bottling.
- Record the lot number of every malt and hop sack used in a batch, captured
  when the sack is opened.
- Print the batch number and bottling date on every bottle label at the
  bottling run.
- Given a batch number (read off a bottle), show the batch and every sack lot
  that went into it.

## Non-goals
- Inventory or stock levels, ordering, costing.
- Recipe management or brewing calculations.
- Anything customer-facing.

## Anti-goals
- Typing lot numbers by hand on the brew floor. Brewers' hands are usually
  wet. If capture needs typing, the design has failed even if it works.
- Disturbing the existing taproom tab system.

## Constraints
- Existing app: small Flask app with SQLite, on one Raspberry Pi in the
  office. It currently handles taproom tabs.
- An existing label printer is used at bottling.

## Approaches
1. **Extend the existing Flask app (chosen, builder's call).** Add batch,
   sack-lot and bottling tables to the same SQLite database, plus a few
   pages. A USB barcode scanner works as a keyboard, so "scan" is just a
   focused input field. Trade-off: shares a process with the tab system, so
   changes must not break tabs.
2. **Separate small app on the same Pi.** Clean separation, but two things
   to run, back up and keep alive on one Pi, for no gain at this size.
3. **Off-the-shelf brewery software.** Ruled out: it would not drive the
   existing label printer or live alongside the current app.

## What the owner decided
- A batch runs from mash day to bottling and is the unit of traceability.
- Sack lot numbers are the link from batch to ingredients.
- At bottling, each label carries the batch number and bottling date.
- Lot numbers are scanned, not typed, when a sack is opened.

## Builder's calls (flagged for the owner to check)
- **Scanner:** a USB keyboard-wedge barcode scanner at the brew floor
  station. Scan page has a single always-focused field; each scan attaches
  that sack's lot to the batch currently open, with a big on-screen
  confirmation readable from a distance.
- **Sacks without a scannable lot barcode:** if a supplier's sack has no
  barcode, print our own lot sticker when the sack is received (lot typed
  once, dry, in the office) and stick it on the sack. Scanning on the floor
  then works the same for every sack.
- **Label:** batch number printed both as text and as a barcode, so the
  trace page can be opened by scanning a bottle.
- **Reverse lookup:** a lot number shows every batch that used it (one
  query, for supplier recalls).
- **Isolation:** batch tracking lives in its own Flask blueprint and its own
  tables. It touches no tab code. Units: data model; scan capture; bottling
  and label printing; trace lookup. Each is testable alone.

## Left to the builder
- Exact table layout, page design, scanner model, label layout within the
  printer's limits, and how the printer is driven from the Pi.
```

I've written the design to `specs/batch-tracking.md`. Everything you told me is recorded as yours.

A few things you didn't specify, so I made the call. They're flagged in the doc so you can check them:

- **How it's built:** batch tracking goes into the existing taproom app on the Pi, kept separate from the tabs code. Running a second app, or buying brewery software, would add upkeep for no gain at your size.
- **Scanning:** a cheap USB barcode scanner at the brew floor station.
- **Sacks without a barcode:** if a supplier's sacks don't have a scannable lot barcode, we print our own sticker when the sack arrives. The lot number gets typed once, in the dry office, never on the floor.
- **Labels:** the batch number also goes on the label as a barcode, so scanning a bottle pulls up its trace.
- **Recalls:** you can also look up a lot number to see every batch that used it, for when a supplier recalls something.
